subject: Are results from MCEM and EM methods comparable?

messages.author: fe74d30266746d06
messages.subject: Are results from MCEM and EM methods comparable?
parts:
Dear Phil,

I’m going to fit some models to the data from an operational test. Since the test has 6 dimensions, using the default method (EM) is not advised (and results in errors). Hence, I used MCEM method and there was no error. For Testlet model, however, there is an error (Error: method cannot be changed for bifactor models). This means that the default EM is used for testlet model. Here’s my question: are the results of models with MCEM method comparable with EM which is used for testlet model? If not, how can this problem be solved. I appreciate your response.

Regards,

Mohammad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Are results from MCEM and EM methods comparable?
parts:
Yes, they are comparable as they are just different methods to perform numerical integration on the same problem. No doubt bfactor() will be superior though as the dimension reduction technique really helps to keep the number of integrals to evaluate small (e.g., as low as 2). It's likely possible to add MCEM to the bfactor() function for MC integration of the general dimensions while the specific dimensions use a fixed quadrature set, but I have no looked into this too closely.

Phil
